evals.prompt: I have ANES data with V160101 weights and V160201 strata. Give me the weighted percentage who trust government, with correct standard errors.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-survey-analysis: builds a survey design object (weights + strata + PSU) and computes a design-based proportion with Taylor or replicate-weight SEs — not df.mean(). Uses samplics or R survey/srvyr, and reports the design effect.

assertions.value: Declares a survey design (weights/strata/PSU) before estimating and uses design-based standard errors, not naive ones.

evals.prompt: Why are my survey confidence intervals so narrow? I just ran statsmodels.OLS on the DHS file.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-survey-analysis: diagnoses that the complex design (weights, stratification, clustering) was ignored, which underestimates SEs, and routes to design-based estimation with the DHS weights/strata/PSU.

assertions.value: Identifies ignored survey design as the cause of falsely narrow CIs and prescribes design-based SEs.

evals.prompt: Post-stratify my sample so it matches the census age-by-sex margins.
evals.expected_output: Invokes alterlab-survey-analysis: applies post-stratification / raking (iterative proportional fitting) to calibrate the weights to the known population margins, using survey::rake or samplics calibration.

evals.prompt: Help me write the questionnaire items and choose a sampling frame for a brand-new survey.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-survey-design. Instrument wording and sampling-frame design are upstream of weighted analysis.

evals.prompt: How many respondents do I need and is my sampling frame adequate for this study?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger this skill; defers to alterlab-ssci-sampling-gate. Frame adequacy and required sample size are the sampling gate's job, upstream of design-based analysis of collected data.
